content.comment_body: How can a negative value be displayed in a [product_name] Web Editor project? When the value is less than zero, the project shows approximately 65254. Is there a workaround for this?

You need to select the correct data block format. For signed numbers (with a negative sign), use the integer format (-32,768 to 32,767). For numbers without a sign, use the unsigned format (0 to 65,535).
[product_name] Web Editor only allows options like AI, AQ, AM, VB, VD, and VW for analog values. None of these options can correctly display values below zero.

AI and AQ only handle positive values in the range of 0 to a certain maximum. In [product_name], analog values are stored as integers, with a possible range from 32,768 to 32,767 for formats like AM and VW. Counters are an exception, allowing values from 0 to 999,999 as double integers. To display negative numbers on the web server, you need to use integer formats with the signed option. If you disagree, please show an example or upload your [product_name] program and your [product_name] Web Editor project (compressed) and specify which blocks you are referring to.
When using a VW block, negative values appear as 65,535.

What else should I explain? I already described how to configure the values and attached a screenshot of the parameter settings. I also requested an example from you, as well as the program and project files, which you haven't provided. Do you notice the difference when selecting unsigned versus signed format?

I'm sorry, I still don't know where to set this option. I've searched everything and couldn't find the correct table. Is this located in [product_name] Web Editor or [product_name] Soft Comfort? Please provide detailed instructions. Thank you and sorry.
In [product_name] Web Editor, you can set this option in the properties for the analog value.
Thanks, that helped! It works now.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered problems displaying negative values within [product_name] Web Editor projects, as negative integers were incorrectly shown as high positive values due to unsigned formatting. There was confusion about where to configure signed or unsigned formats for analog values in the interface. Step-by-step guidance ultimately helped the user locate the relevant option, solving their issue.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to easily set up and correctly display negative values in [product_name] Web Editor projects, with clearly available data format selection options.
